statement: A BST is given as: a line with n, then a line of n level-order entries where -1 marks an absent child; each placed node consumes the next two entries as its children. All stored values are distinct. Print the minimum and the maximum stored values, separated by a space. The invariant makes both walks trivial: keep stepping left and the last node before the pointer falls off holds the minimum; keep stepping right for the maximum. No comparisons with the values are needed - the direction alone is the algorithm.
constraints: Values are positive; -1 marks an absent child.

example.why: The leftmost node is 2 and the rightmost is 14; inorder confirms: 2 5 7 8 12 14.

hint: Two loops of one line each: follow left until null, follow right until null.
mistake: Scanning every node for min and max - that works on any tree, but here it ignores the invariant's gift.
